video_caption: The video segment opens at night (0:05) with a group of people marching, some carrying lit torches, as the text "OUT of FRAME" and "FEE presents" is overlaid, along with the caption "We all live in a world where tons of people believe stuff". The scene transitions to a daytime protest (0:06), with more people marching, some holding red and black flags, one with a red star. A CNN news banner appears, reading "WHAT IS ANTIFA? INSIDE THE GROUP THAT CLASHED WITH NAZIS IN CHARLOTTESVILLE", while the bottom caption continues "and hold opinions and values that we think are just...". A man wearing a helmet and goggles is seen speaking (0:09) before cutting to two men walking in a public space, one in a red t-shirt with a symbol, as the caption finishes "...Stupid." (0:10). The video then shows a large fire burning in a street at night (0:12), with a crowd around it and a white object with "MILO" written on it engulfed in flames, the CNN banner reappears. This is followed by a close-up of people wearing red hoods or balaclavas and sunglasses (0:13), one with a white star and hammer/sickle symbol on their chest, with the text "Or even worse... Evil.". The scene shifts to another group marching (0:16), some in helmets, carrying a black flag, a red flag, and a Confederate flag, one person identifiable as "PRESS". A man in a suit is shown walking (0:17) before a brief, chaotic shot of people running and a car driving rapidly into a crowd, scattering people (0:20), with the text "Do we all just escalate the war until somebody gets seriously hurt? Or... Killed?". The segment concludes with a man in military-style gear and a gas mask apprehending another man in a bandana and t-shirt (0:26), surrounded by others in similar gear on motorcycles, and debris on a street (0:28), as the captions state "Obviously, that's not helpful." and "The question remains." respectively, both with a "FEE" logo.

The video begins with yellow text overlayed on a blurry, dark background, asking, "When people believe in wrongheaded or terrible things, how do we actually persuade them to stop believing the bad ideas, and get them to start believing in good ones instead?" The blurred background shows a person in a purple and red garment. This transitions to a slightly clearer shot of a man with dark skin, a beard, and a mustache, wearing a blue shirt and dark pants, sitting relaxed on a park bench in front of a large brick building, likely a university, with green grass in the foreground, as the text reveals, "One incredible man named Daryl Davis might have the answer." The scene then quickly cuts to a close-up of Daryl's smiling face, followed by him shaking hands warmly with another person (whose back is to the camera) inside a room with a mural on the wall. Next, Daryl, now wearing a light brown button-up shirt, is seen holding up a black and white photograph for someone off-camera, with the iconic Washington Monument and Reflecting Pool visible in the background, as the text states, "Daryl is the subject of a fantastic documentary called 'Accidental Courtesy', directed by Matt Ornstein." This leads to a title screen with the words "ACCIDENTAL COURTESY" in large white letters, with "DARYL DAVIS," and "directed by Matt Ornstein." below it, set against a bright blue sky with a distant airplane. The segment concludes with Daryl, now in a black shirt, walking with a serious expression down a narrow alleyway adorned with colorful graffiti and murals.

The video segment opens with Daryl, a man with dark skin wearing a light brown shirt and striped tie, playing a black grand piano and speaking into a microphone. A text overlay states: "For the past 30 years, Daryl has been traveling the country as a musician engaging in conversations and even forming friendships with members of the Ku Klux Klan." This is followed by a close-up of his hands on the piano keys, then a scene of Daryl in a black jacket conversing with another man on a city street, and then Daryl, now in a purple shirt, at a table with two other people in a meeting room adorned with American flags. The scene transitions to Daryl in a blue shirt shaking hands and embracing a man dressed in a purple Ku Klux Klan robe with a pointed hat, identified as "FRANK ANCONA Imperial Wizard." Next, Daryl sits on a porch, talking to a man who covers his face with a white pillow, as yellow text asks: "What is it that compels someone to sit down and talk to their worst enemies... instead of fighting?" The video then cuts to Daryl, now on a stage in a light purple shirt, passionately asking, "How can you hate me, when you don't even know me?" The segment concludes with close-ups of an attentive audience, including an older man with glasses, as Daryl's narration states, "Throughout my life, I've been looking for an answer to that." Logos for "FEE", "Y", "INDEPENDENT LENS", and "PBS" appear at various points.

The video opens with a dark, blurry shot showing a man with a mustache in a striped shirt on the left and a person in a white Ku Klux Klan hood and robe with a red KKK emblem on the right, separated by a flaming cross. The text "So I began seeking out members of the Ku Klux Klan." appears at the bottom. The scene then zooms into a closer view of the flaming cross, which appears stylized, followed by a shot where the text "KLAN We Talk?" appears above the cross, with "It's a great question." below. The video transitions to a medium shot of a man with dark skin, a mustache, and short dark hair, wearing a light purple collared shirt and a patterned tie, speaking and gesturing with his right hand in what appears to be an indoor setting with wooden barrels in the blurred background. The text "And to find out, Daryl went on a mission to seek out and engage with high ranking members of the KKK." is displayed. Next, an interior car shot shows the same man in profile, driving, with the street and other vehicles visible through the windshield. The video then shows two still photographs: the first depicts a light-skinned man in a green KKK robe with an emblem and a dark-skinned man in a pink shirt holding a similar emblem, standing against a brick wall with a partially visible "LET GOD" banner. The second photograph features the dark-skinned man with a beard and a maroon shirt, with his arm around a light-skinned man in a black shirt and cap, standing outdoors in front of a Confederate flag and a KKK flag. The text about Daryl's mission continues throughout these last three shots.

The video segment opens in a diner with a dark-skinned man in a light brown shirt sitting across a table from a bald, light-skinned man in a black uniform, identified by an on-screen text as "JEFF SCHOEP Commander National Socialist Movement." Behind them, a wall is adorned with numerous framed black-and-white pictures. The scene transitions to newspaper clippings, first showing "The Frederick Post" with the headline "An improbable friendship" and a sub-headline "Black musician, KKK leader pals despite differences," alongside a photo of a man in a Ku Klux Klan robe standing next to a dark-skinned man. Another clipping is titled "Understanding the Klan" with the text "Black man makes it his mission to change leaders' hearts," featuring a photo of the dark-skinned man and a KKK hood. A close-up highlights the sentence: "Davis and Grand Dragon Kelly became so close that Kelly named Davis his daughter's godfather." The scene then shifts to a dark outdoor setting where a man in a white robe, later identified as Tom Robb, holds a large burning torch, followed by the same man, now in a suit and glasses, speaking in a meeting room with an American flag and another flag (possibly Arkansas) in the background. He is then seen sitting at a table with a woman and the dark-skinned man (Daryl Davis), who is wearing a light purple shirt. Daryl Davis, now in a light blue shirt, is then shown sitting in a chair in what appears to be a dressing room with vanity lights and posters. The segment concludes with a moving shot of green trees against a cloudy sky. Throughout the video, text overlays provide narration and dialogue, including "he's had countless conversations," "and as unlikely as it seems now considers a number of them to be... his friend," "DARYL: Tom Robb would tell you that he is not my friend. He'll make that very clear to you. I am Tom Robb's friend. And I feel that one day, he will come around." The "FEE" logo is visible in the bottom right corner of several frames.

The video segment opens with a close-up of a man with dark skin, dark hair pulled back, and a mustache, wearing a light purple collared shirt. He is speaking, with his mouth slightly open and eyes downcast, against a wooden paneled wall. The on-screen text reads: "Daryl might say that he's not really even doing anything special". The scene then widens to show the man sitting in a dark leather armchair, gesturing with his left hand, in a room with wooden walls, bookshelves filled with photos, a lamp, and a piano. The text continues: "besides treating people with respect and kindness." The perspective shifts to show the man in a maroon shirt sitting on a sofa, looking at a woman with short brown hair, wearing a blue shirt and a beige vest. A lit Christmas tree is visible between them. The woman is then shown in a close-up, looking off-screen with a thoughtful expression, with a piano in the background. She says, and the text displays: "I guess that's true." The scene abruptly transitions to an outdoor protest or march. A large crowd of diverse people fills the street, many holding signs. A prominent black banner with white text reads: "AGAINST WHITE SUPREMACY" (English translation: "AGAINST WHITE SUPREMACY"), featuring an anarchist 'A' symbol within a circle. The text "Yet..." appears as narration begins. The final shot is a close-up of a few individuals at the protest; a person in a black cap and sunglasses, wearing a patterned shirt, speaks into a microphone held by an unseen person. Beside them, a man in a black beanie and t-shirt with a white graphic looks upwards. The on-screen narration concludes: "It's still something almost no one else has the courage to do, even when the risks are considerably lower." The RT logo is visible in the bottom left corner of the protest scenes, and a 'Y' logo in the top right of the initial interview scenes.

The video opens with rapid cuts of various interactions: two men shaking hands in a diner, then two men gesturing towards each other across a table in a dimly lit bar, followed by a dark-skinned man in a blue shirt shaking hands with a light-skinned man in a purple robe. The text overlay during these scenes states, "But Daryl's approach has a lot of empirical support from the neuroscientists & psychologists who study persuasion." The scene then transitions to a split screen showing a man sitting at a desk on the left and a book cover titled "THE EMOTIONAL BRAIN" on the right, still with the same text overlay. This is followed by a series of brain images, first an MRI-like scan with the text "Dornsife Imaging Center hanna damasio," then an anatomical drawing highlighting the "Amygdala," and finally a pulsating brain scan. During these brain-related visuals, the subtitle explains, "Just like how we know from psychological studies that people's amygdalas (the part of the brain that processes raw emotions) can actually hijack their rational minds and create a fight or flight response when they feel threatened or attacked." The video then shifts to a bustling protest scene where people, some wearing helmets and face coverings, push against a barricade, with the subtitle continuing. This is succeeded by screenshots of academic articles: one titled "Study Shows a Bias for Evidence of What We Want to Be True" and another "Biased Assimilation and Attitude Polarization," explaining how presenting conflicting facts can "backfire, causing people to cling to those beliefs more tightly after they've been presented with contrary evidence." Accompanying these explanations are clips of a young woman in a red "MAKE AMERICA GREAT" hat cheering in a crowd, and a CNN news segment titled "WHAT IS ANTIFA? INSIDE THE GROUP THAT CLASHED WITH NAZIS IN CHARLOTTESVILLE," showing masked protesters facing riot police and marching. The video concludes with a sequence of two men (one in a suit, one in a purple shirt) talking in an office, two men shaking hands in a busy indoor setting, two men shaking hands outdoors in front of a brick wall, and finally two men conversing under an urban overpass, all while the subtitle reads, "We also know a lot about how to talk to people in ways that are actually persuasive."

The video segment opens with a white background where a hand is drawing a list titled "6 SHORTCUTS" in bold red text. The handwritten list includes "1. RECIPROCITY", "2. SCARCITY", "3. AUTHORITY", "4. CONSISTENCY", "5. LIKING", and "6. CONSENSUS". To the left, a cartoon drawing of a hand giving a thumbs-up and a road sign pointing left with the text "SHORT CUT" are visible. Below the drawing, a caption reads: "In Robert Cialdini's book, "Influence", he describes what he calls the "Principles of Persuasion"." This transitions to a scene of a man in a white, pointed KKK-style hood and robe speaking into a microphone outdoors, with another man in military attire behind him. The caption continues: "and it's based on the idea that people feel obliged to treat you the way you treat them." This cuts to a man with dark skin, wearing a white shirt, listening intently outdoors, then to a framed photograph showing the KKK-robed man with his arm around the dark-skinned man. An overlay identifies the KKK man as "ROGER KELLY Imperial Wizard of the Invisible Empire". The scene changes to the KKK-robed man and the dark-skinned man sitting together in a studio setting, seemingly in conversation. The caption is now truncated to "So...". The video then transitions to a dimly lit bar where the dark-skinned man, now in a purple shirt, is engaged in conversation with another man across a table with beer bottles. The caption reads: "If you treat them with kindness and humility," This is followed by a scene in a crowded, dimly lit outdoor setting at night, where a young Black man in a black cap and jacket is animatedly speaking to an older white woman with gray hair and glasses. The caption changes to: "On the other hand," and then to: "if you treat them with contempt, well..." as the interaction continues and the young man turns his head. The final scene shows the question "What do you think?" displayed over the blurred image of the crowd.

The video opens with a dark-skinned man with a mustache, wearing a purple shirt, speaking directly to the camera, looking earnest. He states, "DARYL: While I don't support any racist agenda or supremacist agenda, whether it's black supremacy or white supremacy, or whatnot," (English: DARYL: While I don't support any racist agenda or supremacist agenda, whether it's black supremacy or white supremacy, or whatnot,). The scene then briefly cuts to a dark-skinned woman with curly hair, in a green shirt, listening intently, before returning to the man who continues, "I do support their right and their freedom of speech. And their right to express their views. And in doing so, guess what, they reciprocate it." The scene transitions to a light-skinned man in a white Ku Klux Klan hood and green sash in close conversation with the dark-skinned man in a white shirt, with the text "Another principle Cialdini describes is the idea of 'liking'." The man in the KKK hood then looks up with an intense expression, with a Confederate flag visible in the background, as the text continues, "It's almost too obvious, but it turns out that if someone likes you personally,". This is followed by a still image of a younger light-skinned man in a suit holding a rifle, with a Confederate flag behind him, and then two men, one in a vest and purple shirt and the other in a dark jacket, walking towards the Lincoln Memorial, with the text stating, "and believes that you like them,". The segment concludes with a light-skinned man in a brown jacket over a red shirt speaking into a microphone on a stage, and then outdoors in a light gray shirt with a news overlay that reads "A FORMER LEADER OF THE KKK IS TRYING TO STOP RALLY" (English: A FORMER LEADER OF THE KKK IS TRYING TO STOP RALLY) and "PROMOTING PEACE" (English: PROMOTING PEACE), as he finishes the thought, "it's easier to convince them that your way of thinking is worth considering."

The video begins with a wide shot of two men, seen from behind, overlooking the Washington Monument and Reflecting Pool, as text appears stating, "One easy step towards being liked is to listen to others and find common ground through shared interests." This transitions to a close-up of piano strings, then a man in a purple shirt wearing headphones, intently focused. The text elaborates, "This can be a bridge - or a shortcut - to getting other people to see you as a friend." Subsequent scenes show two men, one in a blue jacket and the other in a black jacket (Daryl Davis), smiling and conversing on a tour bus, then standing in front of the White House. Next, Daryl Davis, in a blue shirt, shakes hands with a man in a purple satin robe, who holds a "Traditionalist American Knights of the Ku Klux Klan CERTIFICATE OF FRIENDSHIP" presented to "Daryl Davis," recognizing his friendship and contributions. The text then adds, "Or, even better, part of their tribe." A book cover titled "KLAN-DESTINE Relationships," featuring a burning cross and Daryl Davis shaking hands with a robed KKK member, appears as the text questions if Davis could have anything in common with a KKK member. Daryl Davis, now performing with a singer, states, "But... That's not true." He then sits for an interview, explaining to a woman with curly hair that spending five to ten minutes with an "arch-enemy" reveals commonalities, and as these commonalities are built upon, "The things you have in contrast, like skin color, begin to matter less and less." The video concludes with shots of a man (likely Davis) handling a purple, star-embroidered satin robe, then a white KKK hood, and finally a red flag with a KKK symbol, implying these were given to him, as the text reads, "Over time, forming relationships with members of the Klan has had an interesting side-effect," followed by grainy television footage of KKK members and the text, "In the last couple decades."

The video segment opens with a dark-skinned man in a purple shirt folding a white garment in a rustic wooden room. The text "over 200 of America's most ardent white supremacists have hung up their robes and hoods for good." appears on screen. This transitions to close-ups of old newspaper headlines, including "top KKK leader quits, may run for gover" dated "JULY 10, 1999, ANNAPOLIS, MD," and "Candidate sorry for past," reinforcing the theme of former white supremacists. The scene then shifts back to the same man in the purple shirt, now in a dimly lit storage area, hanging various white robes with pointed hoods, typical KKK regalia, on a clothing rack, with additional robes in green and white visible. He is next seen holding up one of the white robes with green trim in a brighter indoor setting, and the text continues, "And in a lot of cases, these individual conversions have much bigger consequences." A close-up reveals two distinct patches on the robe: one with a cartoonish figure in a sombrero within a green circle, and another red circular patch with a white four-pointed cross and a teardrop shape. Following this, an elderly Black woman in a pink striped dress is seen smiling and hugging a white man in a white t-shirt outside a brick house. The video concludes with a dark-haired woman speaking into a microphone at a wooden podium, with an American flag and another flag in the background, and the text finishes, "and may end multi-generational cycles of bigotry."

The video segment opens with a shot of a television screen displaying a vintage talk show. On stage, a man with a mustache (Geraldo Rivera) in a suit holds a microphone, next to a man with a beard and suspenders. Two females, identified by on-screen text as "ERICA AND ERIN PUIG," have their faces blurred, while one of them, Erin, states, "My name is Erin, and I'm 12." (0:00-0:03). Geraldo then addresses Erin directly, asking, "So, what do you think about your parents belonging to these organizations?" (0:03-0:06). Erin's blurred face is shown as she replies, "I think it's fine" (0:06-0:08), prompting Geraldo to ask, "Why, sweetie?" (0:08-0:10). Erin then articulates, "Well, I mean, they're allowed to like their race, they're allowed to be proud of who they are too" (0:10-0:12). A cut shows a serious-looking African American man in a suit as Geraldo's voiceover asks, "Are you going to be a member of the group also?" (0:12-0:16). Erin, still blurred, responds, "Yes" (0:16-0:17). The scene returns to the talk show stage, with a new speaker named Daryl interjecting, "So now, both daughters are in the Klan" (0:17-0:20), revealing the nature of the organization. Daryl continues, "And their father, he got sentenced to 10 years in a Federal prison" (0:20-0:23), as the man with the beard and suspenders is shown speaking into a microphone. The shot changes to Daryl, a different man in a light yellow shirt and dark tie, gesturing with his thumb as he explains, "So I thought, you know what, I'm going to call Tina, the mother" (0:23-0:26). The mother's face, now clearly visible and identified as "TINA PUIG," appears on screen with a serious expression (0:26-0:28), followed by an animated map highlighting Chicago, Illinois, as Daryl's narration continues (0:28-0:30).

The video opens with an exterior shot of a prison, featuring tall fences topped with extensive razor wire and a prominent guard tower under an overcast sky, with the subtitle "where their father was imprisoned." This transitions to a close-up of coiled razor wire on a fence with the subtitle "So they could visit him." The scene then shifts to an old-fashioned television set displaying a video of two individuals on a stage. A woman with long, curly hair, dressed in a dark top, is speaking at a podium adorned with flowers, while a man in a dark suit stands beside her, smiling and gesturing. Behind them are flags, including what appears to be the American flag, and a banner that reads "MARTIN LUTHER KING JR DAY." On-screen text progresses, with a speaker stating, "And, nobody in the Klan had ever done that for them before." followed by "And so, they had a turnaround." A woman named Tina then speaks, identified by the subtitle "TINA," saying, "Well, my little girls came a long way. You know, no thanks to her father and I. We really did our best to destroy our kids."

The video opens with a man with a mustache in a black shirt, a woman with a blurred face in a light-colored shirt, and another person with a blurred face in an Abercrombie shirt, sitting on a couch. On-screen text identifies them as "ERIN PUIG AND HUSBAND" (English). Subtitles reveal Erin stating, "Me and my husband Harley would like to extend our best wishes to the City of Rockville, MD, as you celebrate the life and legacy of Dr. Martin Luther King. Neither me, nor my family, are members or are affiliated with the Ku Klux Klan anymore." (English). The scene transitions to a dark-skinned man in a light brown shirt and dark tie, speaking and gesturing, with the subtitles continuing his speech. The video then cuts to a CNN news segment with a red banner that reads "WHAT IS ANTIFA? INSIDE THE GROUP THAT CLASHED WITH NAZIS IN CHARLOTTESVILLE" (English). A female reporter sits across from a group of individuals wearing black hoodies and face coverings, some with "ROSE CITY ANTIFA" logos. The subtitles continue, "We live in a time when a lot of people are saying that the only answer to hate and awful ideas..." (English). This is followed by a scene of six men in white Ku Klux Klan robes and pointed hoods holding a Confederate flag in a wooded area. The footage then shows a large group of people, many dressed in black with obscured faces, in an urban setting. This transitions to a street scene with a burning object in the foreground and a damaged police car, with people running nearby. Finally, the segment ends with a close-up of a person's head wrapped in white bandages, with news screens in the background, and the subtitles concluding, "...is to meet them with even more hate, more anger, outrage, and even Violence." (English).

The video opens with animated scenes, first showing a dark, winged creature with red eyes flying over a green, rocky landscape, followed by a silver flying saucer, reminiscent of Rick and Morty, with two figures inside, flying past the creature. A title card for "Scud THE DISPOSABLE ASSASSIN™" then appears on a fiery orange and red background. Throughout these animated segments, white subtitles read: "Recently, Dan Harmon, creator of Rick & Morty, Community, and one of my favorite comic books ever even said the". The scene transitions to a live-action shot of Dan Harmon, a man with a gray beard wearing a dark t-shirt, speaking into a microphone on a stage with a bright blue screen behind him, gesturing with his hands. To his right, another man in a suit sits behind a podium, while a third person with a beard rests their head on their hands at a table to Harmon's left. As Harmon continues to speak, the subtitles add: "that the time for talking was "over". DAN HARMON: We have sat, we have talked, we have argued, we have pondered... The discourse is over." The blue background screen then flickers with static as Harmon gestures, and the subtitle changes to "But...". Finally, the screen turns black with green text appearing: "I disagree." A "FEE" logo is visible in the bottom right corner throughout the video.

The video segment opens with a chaotic street scene where people in civilian clothes clash with individuals in riot gear, with smoke billowing from the ground and a person holding a red, yellow, and blue flag (likely the Venezuelan flag); white text at the bottom reads, "Most of human history is filled with people allowing their arguments to turn into". This transitions to a close-up of a white armored vehicle, marked "GNB" (likely Guardia Nacional Bolivariana), also emitting smoke, as more people clash around it, with the text continuing, "bloody, horrific warfare." A quick cut shows a large machine gun firing from an aircraft, with shell casings ejecting, accompanied by the same on-screen text. The scene then shifts dramatically to a peaceful protest where several people, some wearing purple stoles, sit on a street with yellow lines, clapping and speaking, as the text changes to, "It's only the commitment to dealing with our adversaries peacefully," with an "RT" logo in the bottom left. This is followed by a wide shot of a crowd with a sign reading "NO TRUMP NO KKK NO FASCISM" visible, then a close-up of a sign on a park bench stating "THE ANSWER TO HATE SPEECH IS MORE SPEECH", while the text at the bottom continues, "through free speech and conversation," with a CNN graphic reading "WHAT IS ANTIFA? INSIDE THE GROUP THAT CLASHED WITH NAZIS IN CHARLOTTESVILLE" in the bottom left corner. The video then shows a man with a mustache and beard, wearing a gray suit and red vest, speaking on a talk show set with a "STEVE HARVEY" logo, as the text concludes, "that has allowed us to become more civilized." He is then seen talking to Steve Harvey, who is holding a blue notebook. Finally, the scene changes to a vintage TV screen displaying footage of a man in a white robe (likely a KKK member) talking to another man in a camouflage uniform and black beret, with the caption "DARYL: I did not respect what he had to say." The two men then walk together in the archival footage, and the text updates to "I respected his right to say it."

The video segment features a Black man, identified as Daryl Davis, engaging with individuals and groups with differing views. It begins with a CNN segment showing a smiling white man, Bob White, identified as a "FORMER KLANSMAN," sitting at a kitchen table across from Daryl Davis, who appears serious and attentive. Text on screen reads "CNN OUT IN THE OPEN FRIEND OF THE KLAN PAULA ZAHN NOW." This scene alternates between close-ups of both men as the narrator discusses techniques to convince white supremacists of respect. The video then transitions to Daryl Davis shaking hands with a younger white man, Adam Levin, a "Store Manager," in a retail setting, followed by scenes of various people working in a busy restaurant kitchen and Daryl Davis conversing with an elderly white woman in a diner. A black-and-white photo of Daryl Davis laughing with a white woman is also shown. Subsequent scenes contrast with these interactions, showing a protest with signs like "WHITE SUPREMACY WORKERS WORLD PARTY - PARTIDO MUNDO OBRERO WORKERS.ORG" (Workers World Party - World Workers Party), "ALWAYS ANTI-FASCIST," and "KKK HOMEGROWN TERRORISM," depicting both anti-racist protestors and groups resembling white nationalists with shields and Confederate flags. An aerial view of a chaotic street brawl, with "WHAT IS ANTIFA? INSIDE A GROUP THAT CLASHED WITH NAZIS IN CHARLOTTESVILLE CNN" displayed, is followed by a scene of Daryl Davis standing alone in a field facing a line of people in KKK robes. A split screen shows a younger Daryl Davis next to a KKK member and the older Daryl Davis speaking on CNN, with the text "CNN HOW STRONG IS THE KU KLUX KLAN?". The video concludes with black-and-white photos of Daryl Davis shaking hands with men in KKK robes and the two men from the opening shot, Daryl Davis and Bob White, shaking hands and smiling at a kitchen table, symbolizing friendship emerging from confrontation.

The video segment begins with a black screen, and at the bottom right, the white text "FEE" appears. This transitions into a split screen: the left half is black, and the right half is light gray. On the black left side, white text displays "FEE presents" followed by "OUT of FRAME" in a larger, outlined font, and then "video essays on the intersection of art, culture, and ideas written & edited by sean w. malone". The gray right side features a prominent black "FEE" logo, with "-FEE.org-" beneath it, and to its right, the call to action "Follow us on social media!" accompanied by black social media icons (Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, YouTube) and the handle "@feeonline". The split screen then dissolves into a pure white background as black rectangular shapes animate onto the screen, coalescing to form the "FEE" logo, after which "-FEE.org-" slides in from the right to position itself directly below the logo, remaining static for the rest of the segment.
